\[
\min_{\beta} \sum_{i} \left[ y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1^T (x_i - x) - \beta_2^T \operatorname{vech}\{(x_i - x)(x_i - x)^T\} \right]^2 K(x_i - x),
\qquad
K(x_i - x) = \frac{\sqrt{\det C_i}}{2 \pi h^2} \exp\!\left(-\frac{(x_i - x)^T C_i (x_i - x)}{2 h^2}\right)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(y_i\): The sample at position x_i
- \(\beta_0\): The estimate at x
- \(\beta_1\): The gradient at x
- \(C_i\): The steering matrix of sample i
- \(h\): The global smoothing parameter
- \(s_1, s_2\): The singular values of the local gradients
- \(M\): The number of gradients in the local window, 25

At each pixel x, a polynomial is fitted to the nearby samples y_i by weighted least squares, and the constant term beta_0 is the result. The weights come from a Gaussian kernel shaped by C_i, the steering matrix of each sample. C_i is built from the gradients in a small window around the sample. Its rotation follows the dominant edge direction. Its elongation sigma_i = (s_1 + 1) / (s_2 + 1) grows with the gap between the two singular values of the gradients. Its scale gamma_i = sqrt((s_1 s_2 + 0.01) / M) makes the kernel large in flat areas and small in textured ones. Each iteration estimates the gradients again from the last result.
